short_bio: Supermodel, author, and environmental activist Gisele Bündchen follows an 80/20 plant-forward whole-foods approach documented in her cookbook 'Nourish', eating organic vegetables, whole grains, and beans for 80% of her meals while allowing quality animal proteins such as organic chicken and wild-caught fish for the remaining 20%.

base_diet.name: 80/20 Plant-Forward Organic Whole-Foods Diet
base_diet.description: An 80/20 plant-forward eating style grounded in organic, seasonal whole foods. Eighty percent of meals center on vegetables, whole grains such as brown rice and quinoa, legumes, nuts, and seeds; the remaining twenty percent includes quality animal proteins like organic chicken breast, wild-caught salmon, and eggs. Refined sugar and processed foods are excluded entirely.
base_diet.philosophy: Gisele prioritizes organic, seasonal produce and whole, minimally processed ingredients. Her approach is documented in her cookbook 'Nourish' and emphasizes eating in harmony with the environment: abundant plant foods form the foundation, with moderate animal protein used as an accent rather than the centerpiece.

recipes.title: Tropical Green Smoothie
recipes.description: A vibrant fruit-and-greens blended breakfast with banana, mango, spinach, and chia seeds — Gisele's style of starting the day with plant nutrition.

instructions.text: Add all ingredients to a high-speed blender.
Blend on high until completely smooth, about 60 seconds. Add more coconut water if too thick.
Pour into a glass and serve immediately.

recipes.tips: Use fully ripe frozen banana for natural sweetness without added sugar. Spinach blends in without altering flavor.

recipes.title: Avocado and Egg Toast on Ezekiel Bread
recipes.description: Two organic eggs with creamy mashed avocado on toasted Ezekiel bread, finished with pumpkin seeds and fresh herbs — a nourishing brunch staple.

instructions.text: Toast two slices of Ezekiel bread until golden and crisp.
Meanwhile, cook two eggs to your liking — poached or fried in a small amount of avocado oil.
Mash the avocado with a squeeze of lemon, sea salt, and black pepper. Spread onto the toast.
Top with the eggs, scatter pumpkin seeds and fresh cilantro over the top, and serve.

recipes.tips: Ezekiel bread is best kept frozen for freshness — defrost slices directly in the toaster.

recipes.title: Organic Chicken Bowl with Brown Rice and Roasted Vegetables
recipes.description: An 80% vegetable plate with roasted broccoli, sweet potato, zucchini, and bell pepper over brown rice, topped with a simply seasoned organic chicken breast.

instructions.text: Preheat oven to 400 F. Cook brown rice according to package directions.
Toss broccoli florets, cubed sweet potato, sliced zucchini, and bell pepper strips with olive oil, garlic powder, cumin, sea salt, and black pepper. Spread on a baking sheet in a single layer.
Roast vegetables for 25 minutes, flipping halfway, until caramelized at the edges.

While vegetables roast, season chicken breast with paprika, sea salt, and black pepper. Cook in a lightly oiled skillet over medium heat for 6 to 7 minutes per side until cooked through. Rest 3 minutes before slicing.
Divide brown rice between bowls, arrange roasted vegetables alongside, and top with sliced chicken. Squeeze lemon over everything and garnish with fresh parsley.

recipes.tips: Cook a double batch of brown rice to use throughout the week. The 80/20 plate ratio means vegetables should visually outnumber the protein on the bowl.

recipes.title: Dark Chocolate and Almond Energy Snack
recipes.description: A handful of raw almonds paired with two squares of dark chocolate — a satisfying whole-foods treat that avoids refined sugar.

instructions.text: Measure almonds and chocolate into a small bowl or snack bag. Pair and enjoy.

recipes.tips: Choose dark chocolate with at least 70% cacao to keep added sugar minimal. Pair with a few walnuts for extra omega-3s if desired.

recipes.title: Herb-Baked Salmon with Quinoa and Mixed Greens
recipes.description: A light, omega-3-rich dinner: wild-caught salmon fillet baked with fresh herbs, served alongside fluffy quinoa and a simple mixed-greens salad dressed with lemon and olive oil.

instructions.text: Preheat oven to 375 F. Rinse and cook quinoa in vegetable broth according to package directions, about 15 minutes.
Place salmon fillets skin-side down on a parchment-lined baking sheet. Drizzle with olive oil and lemon juice, scatter fresh dill and parsley over the top, and season with sea salt and black pepper.
Bake salmon at 375 F for 14 to 16 minutes until it flakes easily with a fork.

Toss mixed greens with a drizzle of olive oil, fresh lemon juice, sea salt, and sliced cucumber. Divide quinoa between plates, add the greens alongside, and place a salmon fillet on top. Garnish with pumpkin seeds.

recipes.tips: Cooking quinoa in vegetable broth instead of water adds depth. The salmon is ready when it turns opaque and the thickest part flakes with gentle pressure.
